title: Grumpy Bookstore Owner
summary: Given an integer array customers where customers[i] represents the number of customers arriving at the start of the i-th minute, and a binary array grumpy where grumpy[i] is 1 if the owner is grumpy during the i-th minute and 0 otherwise, determine the maximum number of satisfied customers.
statement: Given an integer array customers where customers[i] represents the number of customers arriving at the start of the i-th minute, and a binary array grumpy where grumpy[i] is 1 if the owner is grumpy during the i-th minute and 0 otherwise, determine the maximum number of satisfied customers. The owner can use a secret technique to remain not grumpy for a consecutive period of minutes exactly once. When the owner is grumpy, any customers arriving during that minute are not satisfied, but when not grumpy, all customers are satisfied.
constraints: customers and grumpy have equal nonzero length; grumpy values are binary.
Use the technique for one consecutive window of exactly minutes.
reference_solution:
def maximum_satisfied_customers(customers, grumpy, minutes):
 baseline=sum(c for c,g in zip(customers,grumpy) if g==0);extra=sum(customers[i] for i in range(minutes) if grumpy[i]);best=extra
 for right in range(minutes,len(customers)):
  if grumpy[right]:extra+=customers[right]
  if grumpy[right-minutes]:extra-=customers[right-minutes]
  best=max(best,extra)
 return baseline+best

hints: Customers from non-grumpy minutes form an unavoidable satisfied baseline.
The technique adds only customers in grumpy minutes inside its window.
Slide a fixed-size window over recoverable counts and retain its maximum, then add the baseline.
Every allowed use is one such window, and baseline customers never depend on its position.
